title: Excel Sheet Column Number
description:
# Excel Sheet Column Number

Given a string `columnTitle` that represents a column title in an Excel sheet, return its corresponding column number.

Column titles proceed as `A, B, ..., Z, AA, AB, ..., AZ, BA, ...`, with column numbers starting at `1`.

For example:

```
A -> 1
B -> 2
C -> 3
...
Z -> 26
AA -> 27
AB -> 28
...
```

## Example 1:

**Input:** columnTitle = "A"
**Output:** 1

## Example 2:

**Input:** columnTitle = "AB"
**Output:** 28

## Example 3:

**Input:** columnTitle = "ZY"
**Output:** 701

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= columnTitle.length <= 7`
*   `columnTitle` consists only of uppercase English letters.
*   The column number represented by `columnTitle` is in `[1, 2^31 - 1]`.

solutions.name: Left-to-Right Horner Accumulation
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan the title from left to right. For each character, multiply the accumulated value by 26 and add the one-based letter value `c - 'A' + 1`.

## Key Insight

This is Horner's rule for positional notation. Each new character shifts the existing prefix one base-26 position to the left, then contributes its own one-indexed digit value.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), where n is the title length.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because only the running value is stored.

solutions.name: Right-to-Left Place Values
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan from the last character to the first. Maintain the current place value, starting at 1 and multiplying by 26 after each character. Add `digit * place` for every position.

## Key Insight

This version exposes the positional weights directly: the rightmost character has weight 1, the next has weight 26, then 26^2, and so on. The letter digit itself is still one-based.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), because every character is processed once.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because only the result and current place value are stored.

solutions.name: Recursive Prefix Fold
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a helper that stores the value of the prefix already read. At each index, multiply that prefix value by 26, add the current one-based digit, and recurse to the next index.

## Key Insight

The recursive state is exactly the same as the iterative left-to-right accumulator. Writing it recursively makes the invariant explicit: `value` always represents the prefix before `index`.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), because the helper visits every character once.
- Space Complexity: O(n), because the recursion stack has one frame per character.

solutions.name: Precomputed Powers Table
solutions.description:
## Approach

Precompute powers of 26 for each position from the right, then multiply each character's one-based digit by the power assigned to its position and sum the products.

## Key Insight

This separates the two ideas in the formula: a character contributes its digit value, and its index determines the power of 26. It is useful for teaching the exact numeric expansion of a title such as `ZY`.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), because powers and contributions are each computed in linear time.
- Space Complexity: O(n), for the powers table.

solutions.name: Digit Lookup Table Fold
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a small lookup table that maps `'A'` through `'Z'` to values 1 through 26. Then perform the normal left-to-right fold using the table value for each character.

## Key Insight

This version makes digit decoding explicit and leaves the positional fold separate. The table is constant size, so it does not change the asymptotic memory usage.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n), because the title is scanned once after initializing a constant-size table.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because the table has exactly 26 entries.

tests.description: Single first column title maps to one.
AA is the first value after Z.
AZ checks a trailing maximum digit.
BA is the first value after AZ.
First three-letter title checks positional accumulation.
First four-letter title checks repeated carries.
Maximum int title checks large base-26 accumulation.
